data.hypothesis: The selected parent creates a region per timestep at a one-thread budget but keeps one persistent team for larger budgets. This candidate changes only the multi-thread region lifetime: it uses a region per timestep for every positive parallel budget while retaining the same row partition, stencil arithmetic, and serial cutoff. At one thread its behavior remains comparable to the parent; at four threads the comparison tests whether six team creations cost more than the persistent region and its inter-step barriers. No speedup is assumed before controller measurement.
data.notes: The measured baseline mean is 0.45749 s; the selected parent is valid at 0.26154 s, and the best recorded candidate is valid at 0.22921 s. These aggregate outcomes do not establish the effect of region lifetime or predict this candidate. It retains the serial path for small work and nonpositive budgets. Controller correctness checks and official one- and four-core measurements are needed; no tests or measurements were run for this proposal.
transformations: Retained the original serial stencil, initialization, six-step ping-pong parity, and small-work serial cutoff.
Retained balanced contiguous row-block ownership based on the actual OpenMP team size and the call's threads budget.
Changed parallel dispatch so every positive parallel budget creates a separate OpenMP region for each timestep, enabling comparison against the parent's persistent multi-thread region.
